paper.title: Offline Training of Language Model Agents with Functions as Learnable Weights
paper.central_claim: Treat an LLM agent’s functions as learnable parameters: AgentOptimizer progressively adds/revises/removes functions from execution histories, with rollback and early stopping, improving unseen downstream task performance without modifying LLM weights.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

sections_read: Opus: complete pinned text read end-to-end (abstract, all sections, tables, appendices) before opening seat records; targeted re-reads for every disputed field

evidence.quote:
1) The execution history of the agents in solving each problem of the training set, including the details of how the agent uses current functions and
2) the final performance over the training data.
evidence.support_explanation: The optimizer sees training traces and scores, rather than only a scalar loss.

evidence.quote:
In particular, we adopt four actions:
1)
add_function
: add one new function that may be useful; 2)
revise_function
: revise one existing function; 3)
remove_function
: remove one existing function; and 4)
TERMINATE
: terminate the function update process.
evidence.support_explanation: Editable non-weight artifacts and action interface are explicit.

evidence.quote: Specifically, at each optimization step, if the latest function update leads to a performance drop on the training set, the AgentOptimizer will withdraw this update.
evidence.support_explanation: Training-set regression gate and rollback; not an independent statistical commit rule.

evidence.quote: For each data type (7 in total), we randomly choose 20 training examples and 80 test examples, and report the accuracy of each data type respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit independent instance split and denominator for MATH.

evidence.quote: Across seven data types, we observed that agent training led to better performance on the test set in most cases (11 out of 14).
evidence.support_explanation: Reported held-out effects include exceptions, not universal improvement.

evidence.quote: Specifically, to investigate (1), we removed roll-back and early-stop and trained the agent until reaching the maximum epoch number.
evidence.support_explanation: Gate-off comparison bundles rollback and stopping; matched optimizer budget is not established.

evidence.quote: To some extent, it represents GPT-4+ agents overfitting to the training set and suffering from a test performance drop while the training performance remains the same.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-observed generalization failure limits safety and transfer claims.

evidence.quote: Different from prior works, our AgentOptimizer updates the function set based on the LLM agent’s execution history of the whole training set, rather than making functions according to individual query-answer pair(s)
evidence.support_explanation: Author-side differentiation from Tool-maker, CREATOR and CRAFT; not independent verification of neighbors.

evidence.quote:
Specifically:
(1) We set the training epoch to 10 for all experiments.
(2) An early stopping criterion was established with a threshold of 10 epochs.
evidence.support_explanation: Concrete horizon; stopping threshold equals maximum epochs, weakening separate attribution to early stopping.

evidence.quote: Even when the batch size is set to 20, which is the same as the training data size in Figure
evidence.support_explanation: Batch-scaling negative result discussed in §3.3.4; no number extracted from inaccessible plot.

evidence.quote: We randomly sampled 100 test examples and 10 training examples. We measured the model performance using accuracy based on the exact match.
evidence.support_explanation: Checkable task metric and sampling denominator. Table 2 train percentages are not all multiples of 10%, an internal reporting inconsistency.

evidence.quote: We observed that the created functions for the three tasks exhibit relatively low complexity, indicating that the functions are reliable.
evidence.support_explanation: Low cyclomatic complexity is not semantic correctness; reliability inference is stronger than this proxy warrants.

evidence.quote: the proposed agent training method could identify the function set
evidence.support_explanation: Assumption A.2 assumes empirical global minimization; theorem does not establish that the practical optimizer achieves it.

evidence.quote: we propose to progressively forge agent’s functions to better solve the downstream tasks instead of modifying the LLM weights.
evidence.support_explanation: 中心主张：改的是 agent 的函数集合（非权重组件），由 LLM 优化器更新。

evidence.quote: our AgentOptimizer updates the function set based on the LLM agent’s execution history of the whole training set
evidence.support_explanation: 与最近邻工具创建方法的差别：依据整个训练集的执行历史迭代更新，而非逐 query 造工具。

evidence.quote: Since the tool-creation procedure is a one-time process that does not include subsequent optimization mechanisms based on training performance
evidence.support_explanation: 作者对 CREATOR/CRAFT/Tool-maker 缺口的界定：一次性造工具、无基于训练表现的后续优化。

evidence.quote: The execution history of the agents in solving each problem of the training set
evidence.support_explanation: 优化器的可见信息：训练集每题的完整执行历史（原始轨迹）与总体表现。

evidence.quote: if the latest function update leads to a performance drop on the training set, the AgentOptimizer will withdraw this update.
evidence.support_explanation: 保留/回退规则：以训练集表现下降为回退条件（选择数据=训练集本身）。

evidence.quote: We set the training epoch to 10 for all experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: 总训练轮数 E=10。

evidence.quote: An early stopping criterion was established with a threshold of 10 epochs.
evidence.support_explanation: 早停阈值 C=10 轮；与 E=10 并用时，早停在算法 2 的 r>C 条件下不可能在 10 轮内触发（我们的推断）。

evidence.quote: For each data type (7 in total), we randomly choose 20 training examples and 80 test examples
evidence.support_explanation: MATH 每类 20 训练/80 测试；样本量很小。

evidence.quote: We randomly sampled 100 test examples and 10 training examples.
evidence.support_explanation: TabMWP 10 训练/100 测试。

evidence.quote: we randomly select 10 questions for training and 100 questions for testing
evidence.support_explanation: GAIA 10 训练/100 测试。

evidence.quote: we observed that agent training led to better performance on the test set in most cases (11 out of 14).
evidence.support_explanation: MATH 上 14 个(类型×agent)组合中 11 个测试集提升，另 3 个未提升；作者自报，单次运行。

evidence.quote: GPT-4+ Agent w/o Agent Training 10.0% 16.0% 30.0% 51.0%
evidence.support_explanation: GAIA/TabMWP 训练前：GAIA 训练 10/测试 16，TabMWP 训练 30/测试 51。

evidence.quote: GPT-4+ Agent w/ Agent Training 30.0% 23.0% 66.7% 56.0%
evidence.support_explanation: 训练后 GAIA 测试 16→23，TabMWP 测试 51→56（各 n=100，+7/+5 个百分点，无区间）。

evidence.quote: agent training without progressive function update even exhibited worse performance than the origin GPT-4+ agent without agent training.
evidence.support_explanation: 对"整体重生成函数集"这一朴素替代的消融：去掉渐进更新反而低于未训练基线，说明更新方式有因果作用。

evidence.quote: we chose three data types of MATH that resulted in the largest performance improvements in training GPT-4+ agent
evidence.support_explanation: 消融只在提升最大的 3 个类型上做（按结果挑选），削弱外推。

evidence.quote: The results indicate that both GPT-4+ agent and ReAct agent trained with our method outperform tool-creation methods in most cases.
evidence.support_explanation: 作者对 Table 4 的总结。

evidence.quote: GPT-4+ Agent w/ Agent Training 60.0 % 66.25% 66.6% 56.0%
evidence.support_explanation: Table 4 中 GPT-4+ 训练后 MATH-Test 66.25%，低于同表 CREATOR 75.0%/CRAFT 73.8%（表中数值）；ReAct 77.5% 略高于 CREATOR；"most cases"部分被表数据反驳。

evidence.quote: To some extent, it represents GPT-4+ agents overfitting to the training set and suffering from a test performance drop while the training performance remains the same.
evidence.support_explanation: 作者承认在小训练集上出现过拟合：最高测试表现不在最后一轮。

evidence.quote: A significant bottleneck in the agent training algorithm arises from that the size of training data is limited by the LLM context limit.
evidence.support_explanation: 训练数据受优化器上下文长度限制，是方法的结构性边界。

evidence.quote: The results show that large training data does not necessarily lead to test performance improvement in most cases
evidence.support_explanation: 作者自报：简单 batch 扩展无效（负结果）。

evidence.quote: Due to the high cost of OpenAI models, it is impractical to evaluate the method on the complete datasets and therefore we subsample data from these datasets
evidence.support_explanation: 因成本只用子样本评测，未报告训练/评测的具体成本。

evidence.quote: As an initial attempt, our analysis on the generalization bound of the agent training requires the following two strong assumptions.
evidence.support_explanation: 理论附录的两个强假设（训练/测试同分布；训练能找到训练集最小损失函数集），界不能作为本文证据。

evidence.quote: Our observations indicate that the number of successful function calls exhibits significant improvement in most datasets
evidence.support_explanation: 学到的函数被实际调用的次数增加（Table 6）：函数确被后续轮次读取。

evidence.quote: we choose two data types, the only data type that failed to improve the test performance (Algebra)
evidence.support_explanation: Algebra 为测试未提升的典型负例，曲线事后选取。

evidence.quote: Interestingly, for counting and probability problems, when training GPT-4+ agent, the training performance remains the same while test performance improves from 72.5% to 76.3%.
evidence.support_explanation: C.Probability had zero training-set improvement, yet it is one of the three ablation types chosen for 'largest performance improvements' (§3.3.1) — so the ablation subset was picked by test-set gains. Main-table holdout is unaffected (test never drives rollback); the ablation is test-selected.

signatures.object: Persistent callable function set for GPT-4+ / ReAct, not backbone weights
signatures.information: Training questions, generated/ground-truth answers, task success and full execution histories; held-out test tasks are for evaluation.
signatures.operation: Repeated add/revise/remove/terminate actions, up to 3 per update
signatures.output: Named Python functions with description, argument schema, packages and code
signatures.conditions: API LLM supports functions; traces and ground-truth task scoring are available within context.
signatures.selection_rule: Rollback on training regression; Algorithm 2 strict-improvement update; prose and equal-score semantics are not entirely aligned.
signatures.selection_data: 20 MATH examples/category or small GAIA/TabMWP training subsets
signatures.persistence: Current accepted function set and failed-update list; failed list reset after improvement
signatures.later_use: Subsequent epochs and unseen test tasks invoke learned functions
signatures.claimed_effect: Held-out accuracy improvements on most agent/task pairs
signatures.failure_boundary: Overfit, stochastic aggregate regression, large-batch instability, context length; no per-case safety guarantee

gap.author_gap: Manual fixed tool curation is slow and weight finetuning unavailable for proprietary LLMs.
gap.checked_gap: Operationally concrete residual: existing query-level tool generation does not iteratively revise a shared function set from whole-agent histories.

gap.closest_adjacent: CREATOR and CRAFT comparisons in Table 4; GPT-4+ trained agent is worse than CRAFT on MATH (66.25 vs 73.8), so not uniform dominance.

gap.stakes: Reusable functions may reduce repeated code generation and improve closed-API agents.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: a function set learned offline from training-set execution histories, with training-set rollback, improves held-out test accuracy in most (not all) reported cells for two agent types; single runs, small test subsets, no cost ledger.

G.reason: Opus sides with sol. Gap is concrete: hand-crafted or one-shot per-query tools (CREATOR, CRAFT, Tool-maker) are created without optimisation against downstream performance, and two of these neighbours are compared empirically (Table 4). Not 4: executable skill-library neighbours (e.g. Voyager-type libraries) are not covered and the 'train without weights' framing is background (son55's point, which caps G below 4 but does not make the neighbour comparison 'incomplete' at the 2 anchor).

M.reason: Opus sides with sol. Mechanism is reconstructable (full-training-set histories → one of add/revise/remove per step → rollback + failure memory) and its distinguishing predictions against naive alternatives (one-shot regeneration; no rollback) are stated and tested (Table 3). Not 4 because the acceptance signal is accuracy on 10–20 training items (noisy) and authors observe overfitting; son55's gate-noise point is real but the causal logic is not merely partial, so 2 under-rates it.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Actions, inputs, rollback, failure-list write-back and next-epoch read are specified; epochs=10 with early-stop threshold 10 means early stop never fires; no versioning or retirement.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Exact-match accuracy on standard labelled benchmarks; small sub-samples (80/100 test per cell); TabMWP training accuracies (66.7%, 73.3%) are inconsistent with the stated 10 training items.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Store-off (w/o training), rollback-off and progressive-off ablations and two tool-creation baselines exist, but ablations run only on three test-selected types (opus:O01), optimizer compute is unmatched, and Table 4 partly contradicts the summary.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Rollback and early stop use training data only; the disjoint test subset certifies the frozen set; cross-type transfer (Fig. 3) adds evidence. Deductions: same-distribution sub-samples, authors report overfitting, ablation and illustrative types were chosen after seeing test results.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): sample counts and negative cells reported, but every result is a single run without intervals; ±5pp differences at n=80–100 are within noise.

E.cost.reason: Both seats not_reported; re-checked: no optimizer token/call/time or budget-matched comparison anywhere; only a remark that OpenAI cost forced sub-sampling.
